description:
FOUND s491 (Fable, 2026-09-19) by the #1910 review probe (~/pcl-agent-scratch/s491/probes/p1910-moo.pl: stdout == perl cold/warm/warm, stderr carries the line above on EVERY run).  PRE-EXISTING on main 4c6565e5.  The program is right; the noise is on every run of every Moo program, on exactly the machines of the people most likely to try PCL (Class::XSAccessor is a recommended Moo dependency).  Workaround today: MOO_XS_DISABLE=1 (verified: output then identical to perl).

MECHANISM (probed, p-xsload-msg.pl): PCL`s @INC includes perl`s site_perl, so `require Class::XSAccessor` FINDS the .pm, transpiles it, and its `XSLoader::load` dies "Can`t locate loadable object for module Class::XSAccessor in @INC" (no artifact under ~/.pcl-cache/xs/abi-N/ -- nobody ran tools/pcl-xs-install for it, and pclxs is parked).  Moo::_Utils::_maybe_load_module (Moo 2.005005 line 161) treats ONLY /\ACan`t locate \Q$file\E / as "not installed" and WARNS on any other error.  perl itself would print the same warning for a .pm whose .so is missing -- so PCL is perl-shaped for a BROKEN install, but the situation is not a broken install: for PCL the module simply is not available.

RULING (Fable s491; re-raise with the USER only if the bar below cannot be met): an XS module that has no PCL-built loadable object is NOT INSTALLED as far as the program can tell.  Shape, keyed on the MECHANISM, never on a module name (CLAUDE.md 9a):
  1. PCL`s XSLoader::load / DynaLoader bootstrap failure for "no artifact for this ABI" signals a TYPED condition (or a die whose object carries a marker slot) -- it keeps today`s message text when it escapes on its own (a DIRECT `XSLoader::load` call outside a require must read as it does now).
  2. `require FILE` (and `use`), when the load of FILE dies with THAT condition raised from FILE`s OWN top-level load (not from a nested require of a different file that is itself loadable -- decide by the innermost require frame that owns the XSLoader call), re-raises perl`s own not-found text: "Can`t locate Class/XSAccessor.pm in @INC (the module is XS and has no PCL build -- see tools/pcl-xs-install) (@INC entries checked: ...)".  The prefix up to "in @INC" is what the ecosystem greps; the parenthesis is ours and says the truth.
  3. %INC: the failed entry is REMOVED (perl: a failed require deletes it / leaves undef so the next require retries or says "Attempt to reload"); probe what perl does for a die-in-require and match it for this path.  The partially-defined package (subs defined before the XSLoader call) stays, as in perl.
  4. The module cache must not cache the FAILURE as a success or re-transpile on every run for nothing: measure a warm run before/after (this is on Moo`s startup path, #1910`s neighbourhood) -- remember the negative result per process at least.
  5. When a PCL build DOES exist (pcl-xs-install ran), nothing changes: the load succeeds.

PROBE THE BREAKING CASES: (a) `eval { require Some::XS; 1 } or require Some::PP` (the standard optional-XS idiom: must stay silent and fall back -- works today, must keep working); (b) a module that catches the XSLoader failure ITSELF and falls back to pure perl inside the same file (List::Util-style `eval { XSLoader::load(...) }`): the typed condition must NOT escape an inner eval, and the require must then SUCCEED; (c) `use Some::XS;` at file level with no fallback: dies at load with the not-found text, trappable; (d) Params::Util / Class::XSAccessor / Clone under Moo, Type::Tiny (Type::Tiny::XS), JSON::MaybeXS (Cpanel::JSON::XS -> JSON::XS -> JSON::PP chain), Package::Stash (XS -> PP), List::MoreUtils, Ref::Util (Ref::Util::XS -> PP) -- each is the idiom in a different spelling; the CPAN board`s stderr logs say which warn today (grep them for "failed to load" / "loadable object").

BAR: `cl/` runtime (the require path + pcl-xs loader) -> full sweep + the companion legs for comp/require*.t + op/require_errors.t (its snapshot row is s438`s) + the CPAN board diffed by ROWS (the board has Moo-family dists; expect stderr-only movement) + tools/pcl-conform if cl/pcl-xs.lisp moves; guard rows in a Pl/t file using a FIXTURE module under a temp dir whose .pm calls XSLoader::load (never a real CPAN name in Pl/ or cl/); docs: docs/xs-artifact-cache.md (one paragraph: what `require` says when no artifact exists) + ir-spec load model.  Flag in the report if the require path gains a handler frame on the HOT path (it must be on the failure path only).

=== THE NUMBER (s473x, 2026-09-19, Opus; Fable asked for it with #1910) ===

`MOO_XS_DISABLE=1` is the free A/B for the failed Class::XSAccessor load.
Main 4c6565e5, quiet box, fresh PCL_CACHE_DIR per case, six warm runs
(scratch/s473x/probes/p1910.pl in the s473x worktree), program
`package Pt; use Moo; has x => (is=>'rw');`:

    with the XS attempt (default)   run 5 4.419 s   run 6 4.401 s   cold 19.33 s
    MOO_XS_DISABLE=1                run 5 4.300 s   run 6 4.351 s   cold 18.80 s

So the re-attempted load costs **0.05â0.12 s warm** (~1â3 % of the run) and
**~0.5 s cold** (the cold run also transpiles Class/XSAccessor.pm into the
module cache: `XSAccessor.pm` appears in the run-1 build list and disappears
under MOO_XS_DISABLE=1).  It is NOT where #1910's 4 s are â those are the
pack extension load (#1202).


=== DONE (s491a) ===

SHIPPED on the ruling as written.  cl/pcl-runtime.lisp only; guard
Pl/t/require-xs-01.t (16 rows, 2.1 s wall), inverse-verified on an extraction
of 337f6a23 (5 rows FAIL there).

THE SHAPE: XSLoader::pl-load still calls p-die with today's message, plus a
`:die-class 'pcl::p-xs-no-artifact` marker -- p-die learned that marker in the
SAME extractor that already pulled `:loc` (%p-extract-loc -> %p-extract-die-markers,
two call sites; %p-die-error takes the class), so the escaping die keeps p-die's
whole tail: the location suffix, the uncaught-die hook, the exit status, the
trappability.  p-use wraps ONLY p-load-module-cached in a handler-case for that
class and converts it via %p-xs-not-installed, which sets ENOENT and dies
"Can't locate M/Path.pm in @INC (the module is XS and has no PCL build -- see
tools/pcl-xs-install) (@INC entries checked: ...)".  The INNERMOST require frame
wins for free (CL searches handler clusters innermost-first); an inner eval in
the module is innermore still, so a self-falling-back module never reaches us.
Per-process memo *p-xs-unavailable-modules* (rel-path -> T), consulted right
after the %INC check.  NO handler frame on the hot path: one handler-case per
module LOAD, one gethash per p-use.

%INC: PROBED 5.40.3 first (scratch/s491a/probes/p1917.perl.out).  A die-in-require
leaves the entry PRESENT-but-UNDEF and a second require says "Attempt to reload";
a module that was never FOUND leaves NO entry and repeats "Can't locate".  We
present not-installed, so we take the second shape: no entry, same message again.

ACCEPTANCE (the brief's): ~/pcl-agent-scratch/s491/probes/p1910-moo.pl under
`pcl` with a fresh PCL_CACHE_DIR (mkdir -m 700), cold / warm / warm-again --
stdout byte-identical to perl and stderr EMPTY (0 bytes) in all three.  On the
337f6a23 extraction the same three runs each carry 142 bytes of stderr (the
"Class::XSAccessor exists but failed to load" line).  Logs:
scratch/s491a/probes/moo-accept.fix1.log / moo-accept.base1.log.

COST: the failing module is still transpiled ONCE and cached (verified: its
.lisp/.fasl keep their mtime across runs, so every later run is a FASL HIT, not
a re-transpile).  Interleaved warm A/B of the Moo probe, 5 runs each on a box
shared with another agent (load 6.2 -> 3.4): base 7.92 8.13 8.34 8.50 7.92 s,
fix 8.18 8.21 8.51 8.60 8.74 s -- inside this box's noise for this program (the
two acceptance runs on a quieter box read the other way, base 9.98 vs fix 7.67
warm).  No mechanism in the change can cost more than one gethash per `use`
plus one handler frame per module load.

PROBES vs perl 5.40.3 (scratch/s491a/probes/p1917b.{pl,perl.out,s491a-wip.out}),
fixtures under scratch/s491a/fix1917 -- 12 rows.  Four are SAME-as-perl and are
the cases the change would break: a direct XSLoader::load outside a require keeps
the loadable-object text; a module that catches its own failure LOADS with %INC
present; `eval { require XS } or pure-perl` falls back; a module that catches the
failure and then dies of its own reports ITS OWN die.  The rest are the
deliberate divergence, each with perl's broken-install answer beside it.

DOCS: docs/xs-artifact-cache.md gains "Decision 4a" beside Decision 4 (which
stands -- it is about the idiom INSIDE the module); docs/ir-spec.md section 9
gains the normative paragraph.

NOT DONE, and why: DynaLoader::bootstrap is a silent no-op STUB in PCL (it never
fails), so there is no failure there to mark; making it fail is a behaviour
change beyond this task's measured cause and is not attempted.  FILED: #1970
(a die during the load of a :local module prints SBCL's own load-as-source
context note on stderr -- pre-existing, reached by ./runpcl and by any -I
module).
subject: ALPHA-VISIBLE WART: every Moo program prints "Class::XSAccessor exists but failed to load with error: Can`t locate loadable object for module Class::XSAccessor in @INC" on any box where that (very common) XS module is installed for perl -- an XS module with no PCL-built object must look NOT INSTALLED to `require` (design RULED, Fable s491)
